title: V1 inference API compatibility surface, v1alpha1
description: The compatibility target of the user-facing InferOps inference API, the exact endpoint subset V1 serves, the request and response shapes of each one, the capabilities the surface declares rather than assumes, the extension namespace for what the compatibility target does not define, and the mapping from observable runtime behaviour to canonical error codes. This is a decision about shape. Nothing in this repository serves any of it; implementationStatus says so and no row may claim otherwise.

implementationStatus.meaning: The InferOps API in src/inferops/api/ registers every endpoint below and answers it, through the serving adapter it is composed with, and which adapter that is comes from configuration: INFEROPS_SERVING_ADAPTER is required, it selects nothing when unstated, and a real selection whose runtime settings are absent is refused rather than answered with a mock. Nothing in this repository binds a socket: the application implements the ASGI calling convention and no server ships here, so what has been exercised is the application through its own interface and not a network. The canonical error body below is served in full, and every condition this record maps is reachable. Two parts of the decided shape remain deliberately unfinished and each is named where it applies: /metrics publishes no series, and two accepted request members are validated and not forwarded. The telemetry work owns the first, and the second needs a superseding decision on the adapter interface.
implementationStatus.publishedArtifacts: none. No OpenAPI document, no JSON Schema for a request or a response body, and no addition to contracts/ is made by this record or by the component that serves it. Serving a shape is not publishing it as a contract artifact a client may bind to, and D9 stays undecided.

compatibilityTarget.name: The OpenAI HTTP API shape, restricted to a frozen subset
compatibilityTarget.prefixMeaning: The /v1 prefix belongs to the compatibility target's shape and is not an InferOps version claim. InferOps versions this surface through contractVersion, which is inferops.io/v1alpha1 and moves independently of the prefix.
compatibilityTarget.shapeReadFrom: The response bodies recorded in the runtime feasibility record on 2026-08-24. No vendor documentation was read for any of it.
compatibilityTarget.boundedBy: The field lists in this file. Compatibility is a shape borrowed on a date and frozen here; it is not a commitment to track what the upstream surface does next.
compatibilityTarget.specificationBasis: The integration specification prefers a compatible API over an invented one, on the condition that it does not hide behaviour the platform is required to expose, and it allows what the target does not define to live in a namespaced extension. Both halves of that condition are what D1 and D5 are answering.

extensionNamespace.bodyMemberMeaning: One object-valued member carrying everything the compatibility target has no place for. snake_case matches the surrounding body; the x_ prefix marks it as an extension and collides with no member observed in the runtime's own responses.
extensionNamespace.headerPrefixMeaning: The transport metadata the integration specification names for HTTP integrations: request id, correlation id, workload id, workload version, environment. A different namespace from the body member, with a different purpose, and named here so the two are not confused.
extensionNamespace.requestExtensionReason: V1 defines no request-body extension member. Correlation and workload metadata travel in headers, and the integration specification requires that security-sensitive values are validated or injected by a trusted component rather than trusted because a client sent them. A request member a caller fills in would be the wrong place for all of it.

endpoints.servedBy: inferops.api. Validation, translation, the completion body, and the canonical error body in full are served; max_tokens and temperature are validated and not forwarded because the frozen adapter interface carries neither.

endpoints.purpose: The one model this deployment serves, plus the runtime descriptor in the extension namespace.
endpoints.servedBy: inferops.api. The list envelope and the runtime descriptor are served; the capability set is published from what the selected adapter declares, and deterministicSampling is published as null because the frozen adapter interface declares nothing about it.
endpoints.responseShapeNote: The trial called this endpoint and the record shows what came back, but what it shows is the runtime's own model metadata rather than a list envelope. The endpoint was observed; its response envelope was not, and every field of it below is a specification.

endpoints.purpose: Whether the InferOps process is alive. It answers nothing about the model.
endpoints.servedBy: inferops.api. It answers while the model is loading and while the API is draining, which is what makes it a liveness answer rather than a second readiness answer.

endpoints.purpose: Whether the selected adapter can accept an inference request now.
endpoints.servedBy: inferops.api. It is the conjunction of the API accepting work and the selected adapter reporting itself able, and it is false when either half is.

endpoints.purpose: InferOps's own metrics in Prometheus text format, including the request counter the runtime does not have.
endpoints.servedBy: inferops.api serves the route, and it publishes no metric. The accepted telemetry catalog records emissionStatus as nothing-emits and both metrics below as specified; instrumenting this API is the telemetry work, which depends on this API existing. The body names the two metrics and the story that owns them rather than publishing a partial counter that would read as instrumentation.

outOfScope.subject: /v1/completions
outOfScope.reason: The legacy text-completion shape. Serving it doubles the request surface the adapter has to satisfy for one runtime and one chat model, and the chat shape answers the same question.

outOfScope.subject: /v1/embeddings
outOfScope.reason: The pinned model is a chat model. Serving embeddings needs a second model, and ADR 0002 records the selected runtime as a single-model single-process server, so it also needs a second Deployment. Neither is decided.

outOfScope.subject: /v1/responses
outOfScope.reason: A newer upstream shape. Adopting it means tracking a surface that is still moving, which is the thing the frozen-subset decision refuses.

outOfScope.subject: /v1/models/{id}
outOfScope.reason: Retrieving one model by identifier answers the same question as the list endpoint when a deployment serves exactly one model, and V1 serves exactly one.

outOfScope.subject: /v1/audio, /v1/images, /v1/moderations, /v1/files, /v1/batches, /v1/fine_tuning, /v1/assistants, /v1/vector_stores and everything under them
outOfScope.reason: No model, no component, and no storage exists for any of them, and none is in V1 scope.

outOfScope.subject: a graceful-shutdown endpoint
outOfScope.reason: The integration specification requires graceful shutdown or an equivalent, and the equivalent is chosen: SIGTERM handling that flips readiness false, drains what is in flight, and exits. An HTTP endpoint that stops a process would be an unauthenticated remote-stop control on a surface ADR 0008 D4 accepts with no authentication in V1.

outOfScope.subject: /props, /completion, /slots, /infill, /tokenize, /detokenize, /embedding and every other runtime-native path
outOfScope.reason: The runtime's own surface is not proxied. Passing a runtime-specific path through the platform API puts a runtime shape in front of callers and defeats the runtime-neutral adapter interface. Of these, only /props was observed in the feasibility trial; the rest were not enumerated there and nothing here relies on them existing.

capabilities.question: May a caller receive tokens incrementally?
capabilities.basis: V1 has no streaming path. The telemetry catalog already defers inferops_inference_time_to_first_token_seconds for exactly this reason, and this record does not create the path that would un-defer it.
capabilities.runtimeNote: Whether the selected runtime can stream was not exercised by the feasibility trial. This record asserts nothing about it, in either direction.

capabilities.question: Does a response carry the token counts the runtime derived?
capabilities.basis: The trial recorded usage carrying prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and total_tokens on a real completion, and ADR 0002 T5 required it as a blocking threshold.
capabilities.runtimeNote: Reported by the runtime from its own tokeniser. A count InferOps derives by tokenising a prompt itself is an estimate; usage is null when the adapter did not supply it, and is never estimated into a number.

capabilities.question: Does temperature 0 return the same content for the same request?
capabilities.basis: Three runs at temperature 0 returned byte-identical content in the trial. That is one model on one host on one day, and it is the only support this flag has.
capabilities.runtimeNote: Observed, not guaranteed. A caller may not read this as a promise across model, quantisation, thread count, or runtime build.

capabilities.question: May a caller choose between models?
capabilities.basis: ADR 0002 records the selected runtime as a single-model single-process server. One deployment serves one model, so the model field is checked against it rather than used to select.
capabilities.runtimeNote: The trial's GET /v1/models reported exactly one model identifier.

requestFields.v1Behaviour: Compared against the served model identifier. A mismatch is refused with contract-invalid; it is not used to select a model.

requestFields.type: array of objects carrying role and content
requestFields.v1Behaviour: role is one of system, user, assistant. content is a string; the array-of-parts form is outside the frozen subset and is refused with contract-invalid.
Upper bound on generated tokens. A value above the deployment's configured ceiling is refused with contract-invalid rather than silently clamped.
Passed to the adapter. 0 is the value the determinism observation was made at.
Accepted only as false. true is refused with capability-unavailable and a retryable override of false, because retrying does not make a capability appear.

unknownFieldPolicy.meaning: A member of a request body that is not in requestFields is refused, and the refusal names the member. The integration specification requires unknown fields to be handled according to a declared policy; this is the declaration.
unknownFieldPolicy.rationale: Silently ignoring a parameter that changes the result is worse than refusing it. A caller who sends n and receives one choice, or sends stop and receives text past the stop sequence, has been given a wrong answer rather than an error.
unknownFieldPolicy.cost: Clients that send upstream defaults such as top_p, n, presence_penalty, or stop are refused until they stop sending them. That is a real reduction in the reach the compatibility target was chosen for, and it is accepted rather than hidden.
unknownFieldPolicy.rejectedAlternative: Accept unknown members and echo the ignored ones back in the extension namespace. Rejected because it makes the wrong answer the default outcome for a caller who does not read the echo.

responseFields.v1Behaviour: The completion identifier, generated by InferOps rather than passed through from the runtime.
Unix seconds at which InferOps produced the response.
Exactly one element, carrying index, message with role and content, and finish_reason. V1 never returns more than one choice, because n is outside the frozen subset.
prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and total_tokens where the adapter supplied them; null, with the capability flag saying why, where it did not. Never estimated and never zero-filled.
requestId, correlationId, contractVersion, adapterKind, and modelRef. The extension namespace, described in extensionNamespace.
Exactly one element, carrying id, object, created, and owned_by.
The runtime descriptor the integration specification requires, plus the declared capability set.

notPassedThrough.seenAs: b10588-70adb1b4c, in the trial's recorded response
notPassedThrough.reason: A runtime build string on every completion. Runtime identity belongs in the runtime descriptor and in the build-info metric, where it is published once rather than on every response.

notPassedThrough.seenAs: prompt_ms, predicted_ms, and predicted_per_second, in the trial's recorded response
notPassedThrough.reason: Runtime-specific, and a per-request timing figure on a public response is a throughput claim by another route. ADR 0002 already refuses to publish the decode rate it measured.

notPassedThrough.seenAs: cached_tokens, in the trial's recorded response
notPassedThrough.reason: A prompt-cache statistic of the runtime's, and a response member rather than a request one, so the refusal policy for unknown request members does not reach it. It is simply outside the frozen subset for V1 and is not emitted.

errorMapping.condition: The runtime reports not-ready while the model loads.
errorMapping.observation: The control plane recorded a startup probe failing with statuscode 503 during the first load.

errorMapping.condition: The runtime's Service or pod does not accept a connection.
The runtime does not answer within the adapter's deadline.
The caller's own deadline expires before a response is produced.
The request body carries a member outside the frozen subset, a role outside the accepted set, a non-string content, a model that is not the served model, or a max_tokens above the configured ceiling.
The request sets stream to true.
The caller names a contract or API version this deployment does not support.
The runtime answers with a status other than 2xx and other than the 503 that means loading.
The runtime answers 2xx with a body the adapter cannot read into the shape above.

codesNotEmitted.reason: ADR 0008 D4 accepts least exposure at the caller boundary with no authentication in V1. A code for a check that does not run would be a claim that it does.
As for authentication-required. There is no identity to authorize.
No policy engine is selected. The integration specification leaves that choice open and this record does not close it.
V1 has no rate limiter. The runtime's own deferral series is a gauge of instantaneous state, not a limit InferOps enforces.
No budget is enforced anywhere, and ADR 0007 records that every cost figure this project can produce has confidence none.
A release-gate outcome rather than an inference-time condition. It is not this API's to emit.

requestCounting.runtimeGap: The selected runtime exposes no cumulative request counter. ADR 0002 T7 is a blocking threshold and it failed on exactly this, and the record was accepted with the failure argued rather than absorbed.
requestCounting.whyThoseDoNotClose: Both are gauges of instantaneous state. A gauge reading zero between requests cannot be summed, rated, or alerted on the way a counter can.
requestCounting.platformObligation: InferOps receives the requests, so InferOps counts them.
requestCounting.decidedElsewhere: Both metrics already exist in the telemetry catalog with this reason recorded against them. This record adds no metric; it binds the existing entries to this surface and to the error codes above.

adapterConsequences.statement: The API is shaped like the compatibility target at its edge and the adapter interface is runtime-neutral, so the translation happens in the API layer.
adapterConsequences.why: An adapter interface taking a compatibility-target request type would put that shape inside the platform domain, and the architecture's dependency rule forbids exactly that leak.

adapterConsequences.statement: The adapter interface V1-S1-002 freezes exposes one synchronous, non-streaming generate call.
adapterConsequences.why: Streaming is declared false. An interface carrying a streaming method nothing implements is an assumption dressed as a capability.

adapterConsequences.statement: The adapter returns token usage as an optional value rather than a required one.
adapterConsequences.why: A required field forces a mock to invent numbers, and the mock and real boundary names token accounting as one of the properties a mock cannot honestly reproduce.

adapterConsequences.statement: The adapter declares its capability set, and the API publishes what the selected adapter declared rather than a constant.
adapterConsequences.why: A capability that is a constant in the API is an assumption. One the adapter declares is a fact about the thing that will actually serve the request.

adapterConsequences.statement: Every response names the adapter kind that served it, in the extension namespace.
adapterConsequences.why: Which adapter served a response decides what the response may be used to claim. Leaving that to deployment configuration makes the mock and real boundary invisible at the only place a reader looks.

notDecidedHere: The context length, KV budget, concurrency limit, and sampling defaults. ADR 0002 left all four undecided and this record does not fill them in.
The max_tokens ceiling a deployment configures, which depends on the context length above.
Authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and quota at the caller boundary.
Any asynchronous or event-carried inference shape. V1 serves one synchronous request at a time and decides nothing about any other form.
The transport a caller reaches the API over from outside the cluster. The accepted local cluster ships no ingress controller and no load-balancer implementation.
Whether a published contract artifact for this surface is ever added to contracts/, and by what mechanism. The integration specification leaves the publication mechanism open.
